description.value: The Terrace Public Library has served the community since 1929 and has been at its Park Avenue location since 1967, sitting on traditional Tsimshian territories. Beyond standard lending, it offers a notable 'Library of Things' program, a publicly accessible 3D printer, remote printing, and an extensive e-library with dozens of digital databases and streaming resources. It functions as a genuine community hub in a northern BC city that touring cyclists use as a resupply stop on the Yellowhead corridor.

bike_parking_detail: 2 racks within 100m: rack at 52m; rack (covered) at 57m.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content confirms the library's name, address (4610 Park Ave, V8G 1V6), phone (250-638-8177), and email, all consistent with OSM. The website mentions Wi-Fi indirectly (OSM has internet_access=wlan) but does not explicitly confirm it on the website text, so that remains null per rules. No cyclist-specific amenities (bike parking, washrooms, water) are mentioned anywhere in the website content, leaving those fields null.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A functioning public library in a northern BC city is a legitimate and useful stop for touring cyclists on the Yellowhead corridor, even though specific cyclist amenities could not be confirmed from the website. The library's publicly accessible technology (3D printer, remote printing, e-library) and community-hub character make it a worthwhile directory entry pending on-site amenity verification.
